relay_impl_meta_title: Implementing a relay: operators, gateways, conformance
relay_impl_meta_description: The Home-Mandate Relay Specification for operators and gateways: tunnel, pairing, protection levels, five conformance classes and the test tool relay-conformance.
relay_impl_title: Reachable from outside, without having to trust the relay
relay_impl_intro: Most gateways sit behind a router and cannot be reached by agents in the cloud. The Relay Specification defines how a relay makes them reachable under a public name – run by anyone, without the operator being able to read or change what passes. It is a companion specification with its own versions and requires the Home-Mandate Specification {core} or later.
relay_impl_overview_body: The gateway opens a tunnel to the relay itself. The relay passes an agent's TLS connection through the tunnel without opening it: the key exists only in the gateway, and OAuth, the mandate and approvals stay at home.
relay_impl_overview_link: Read Section 1.2 of the Relay Specification
relay_impl_operator_body: Publish your metadata at /.well-known/home-mandate-relay, offer pairing, certificates and both protection levels, and keep the obligations of [Section 7](/relay/v0/#7-operator-obligations). You conform when a test shows it, not when you say so.
relay_impl_gateway_body: Pair with an operator of your choice, keep the tunnel open and watch the Certificate Transparency logs for your name. Classes for gateways follow once gateways implement the specification; the cases for their decisions exist already ([Section 8.5](/relay/v0/#85-cases-for-gateways)).
relay_impl_classes_intro: An operator conforms if it passes all five classes. A claim of conformance names the version, the operator domain, the classes, the manifest of the cases and the date of the test.
relay_class_metadata_body: The metadata document and how it is served, the operator's domains and both protection levels.
relay_class_enrollment_body: Directory, nonces, requests with their errors, pairing, tunnel certificates, ACME support, own-domain names and unpairing.
relay_class_dns_body: The records of the name domain and of a standard name: CAA, A and AAAA, challenge records, TTL and their removal on unpairing.
relay_class_relay_body: The tunnel: TLS, frames, control and data connections, routing by name, the PROXY header, the pinned keys and the denylist.
relay_class_issuance_body: A certificate for a standard name from an allowed CA, the refusals that CAA demands, the SCTs and no other certificate for the name in Certificate Transparency.
relay_impl_cases: cases in {files} machine-readable files, each with a JSON Schema – for operators and for gateways.
relay_impl_classes_note: What no test from outside can check – such as how long an operator keeps data or whether its backup keys are held offline – is part of no class. The report of the test tool lists it, so that a claim of conformance claims no more than was tested.
relay_impl_test_body: relay-conformance plays a gateway and an agent against a live operator: it pairs test installations, sends requests with deliberate defects, opens the tunnel, connects as an agent, obtains a certificate and finally unpairs everything again.
relay_impl_test_more: Every release attaches the tool's report against the reference, with an attestation of its build. [Section 8.3](/relay/v0/#83-live-test) describes the run, [Section 8.4](/relay/v0/#84-access-for-testing) the access an operator gives for it.
relay_cmd_help: The call, the codes, the classes and the exit codes
relay_dl_note: Check files against their SHA-256 checksum. The metadata also has an address of its own: [relay-metadata/v0](/relay-metadata/v0/).
relay_dl_metadata_body: JSON Schema of the document in which an operator describes itself.
relay_dl_enrollment_body: JSON Schema of the messages for pairing, certificates and unpairing.
relay_dl_errors_body: The addresses an operator names in error responses, with their meaning.
relay_errors_title: Error types of the Relay Specification
relay_errors_meta_title: Error types of the Relay Specification
relay_errors_intro: When a relay operator answers a gateway with an error, its "type" member names one of these addresses (Problem Details, RFC 9457). Every address leads here.
relay_errors_source: From the table in [Section 5.1](/relay/v0/#51-directory-nonces-and-requests) of the Relay Specification {version}, in the specification's own words.
